title: Machine learning engineering and MLOps
stage: College AI and machine learning degree
audience: a college student in an artificial intelligence, machine learning or computer science degree program, or an adult studying the same material on their own
purpose: Learn to turn models into reliable systems: framing problems and choosing metrics, data pipelines and validation, reproducible experiments, testing machine learning code, training at scale with accelerators, mixed precision and distributed training, efficient models through quantization, pruning and distillation, deployment for batch and online prediction, monitoring and drift detection, experiments with models in production, and cost, energy, documentation and incident response.
primary_reading: Made With ML by Goku Mohandas (free online course)

weeks.1: Framing ML problems: objectives, metrics and baselines
weeks.3: Reproducible experiments: seeds, versions and tracking
weeks.5: Training at scale: accelerators, memory and mixed precision
weeks.6: Distributed training: data and model parallelism
weeks.7: Efficient models: quantization, pruning and distillation
weeks.8: Deployment: batch and online serving, latency and throughput
weeks.10: Detecting data drift and concept drift
weeks.11: Experiments in production: shadow tests, canaries and A/B tests
weeks.12: Cost, energy, documentation and incident response

blocks.deliverable: Write a data validation function for a training pipeline.
Write tests for a feature transformation and a model wrapper.
Estimate the memory and compute needed to train a model.
Week 7 midterm; quantize weights to 8 bits and measure the error.
Implement a drift check with the population stability index.
Write a postmortem for a model failure.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Production-ready model package: take a model you built in an earlier course, wrap it in a tested Python package with a data validation step, a reproducible training script with fixed seeds and logged settings, a batch prediction function, a drift monitor and a model card, and write a deployment and monitoring plan with the alerts you would set.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
